# Specifies the base image for the build. Ubuntu 22.04 is a stable, general-purpose choice.
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set environment variables for non-interactive package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments to prevent common runtime errors.
# - OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1 and OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1: Required to run MPI as the root user.
# - OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none: Disables a shared-memory mechanism that can fail in some container runtimes.
# - OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=false: Prevents MPI from attempting to use SSH/RSH to launch processes, which is not typical in containers.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1 \
    OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1 \
    OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none \
    OMPI_MCA_plm_rsh_agent=false

# Install essential build tools, compilers, libraries, and certificates.
# - ca-certificates: For secure network communication (e.g., wget, git).
# - build-essential, g++, gfortran, make: Standard compilation toolchain.
# - wget, git: To download source code.
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: The Message Passing Interface (MPI) implementation.
# The command cleans up apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    ca-certificates \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    wget \
    git \
    make \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a temporary working directory for building the application and its dependencies.
WORKDIR /build

# This single RUN command downloads, builds, and installs all dependencies and the main application.
# Chaining these commands into one layer minimizes the final image size.
# The 'set -e' command ensures that the script will exit immediately if a command fails.
RUN set -e && \
    \
    # --- Build and install hypre 2.28.0 ---
    # hypre is a library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers.
    wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf hypre.tar.gz && \
    cd hypre-2.28.0/src && \
    ./configure --with-MPI --disable-fortran --enable-bigint && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    make install && \
    # FIX: Manually copy the library and headers, as 'make install' is incomplete and fails to place them in system paths.
    cp lib/libHYPRE.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp HYPRE_config.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cp hypre/include/*.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Build and install metis 4.0.3 ---
    # METIS is a set of serial programs for partitioning graphs.
    wget https://github.com/mfem/tpls/raw/gh-pages/metis-4.0.3.tar.gz -O metis.tar.gz && \
    tar -xzf metis.tar.gz && \
    cd metis-4.0.3 && \
    make -j$(nproc) OPTFLAGS="-Wno-error=implicit-function-declaration" && \
    cp libmetis.a /usr/local/lib/ && \
    cp Lib/metis.h /usr/local/include/ && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Build mfem 4.7 ---
    # MFEM is a lightweight, general, and scalable C++ library for finite element methods.
    # A shallow clone (--depth 1) is used for the specific tag to speed up the download.
    git clone --depth 1 --branch v4.7 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git && \
    cd mfem && \
    make parallel -j$(nproc) MFEM_USE_METIS_4=YES MFEM_USE_HYPRE=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local && \
    cd /build && \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos application ---
    # Laghos (LAGrangian High-Order Solver) is a miniapp that solves the time-dependent Euler equations.
    git clone https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git && \
    cd Laghos && \
    MFEM_DIR=/build/mfem make -j$(nproc) && \
    \
    # --- Installation and Cleanup ---
    # The final application executable is copied to a system-wide location on the PATH.
    cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ && \
    # The required data files are moved to the final application directory.
    mkdir -p /app && \
    cp -r data/. /app/ && \
    # The temporary build directory is removed to reduce final image size.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /build

# Set the final working directory for the container.
WORKDIR /app

flux-minicluster-manifest.item:
# This MiniCluster manifest is designed for running the Laghos HPC application
# within a single AWS CPU-based Kubernetes node using the Flux Operator.
# It specifies a single-container job with 4 tasks.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # The name of the MiniCluster job.
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment
  # Deploys to the 'default' namespace as requested.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The total number of pods to deploy for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run for the job.
  # The Flux operator will distribute these tasks across the available pods (in this case, one).
  tasks: 4

  # Controls whether the job resources (pods) are deleted upon completion.
  # Set to false to allow for inspection of logs and results after the job finishes.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    # Enforces strict schema validation for the MiniCluster spec.
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The Flux Operator wraps this command
      # with 'flux run', so 'mpirun' or 'flux run' should not be included here.
      command: laghos -m cube_311_hex.mesh

      # The launcher flag MUST be false. When false, the Flux Operator itself
      # is responsible for launching the job via `flux submit` or `flux run`.
      # If true, the entrypoint of the container would be expected to launch the job.
      launcher: false

# Corrects the MiniCluster manifest based on the CRD schema.
# The error "unknown field 'spec.pod.spec'" indicated an incorrect nesting.
# The `nodeSelector` field has been moved to be directly under `spec.pod`.
# Added backoffLimit and restartPolicy as per instructions.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: laghos-cpu-experiment
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Set backoff limit to 1, assuming if it does not work the first time, it will not.
  backoffLimit: 1

  # The total number of pods to deploy for the MiniCluster.
  # Set to 1 to run the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks has been increased to 64.
  tasks: 64

  # Controls whether the job resources (pods) are deleted upon completion.
  # Set to false to allow for inspection of logs and results after the job finishes.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Overrides the default Flux container image, specifying an ARM-based one
  # suitable for the hpc7g AWS Graviton instance type.
  flux:
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Pod-level specifications for scheduling and behavior.
  pod:
    # FIX: The 'nodeSelector' is a direct child of 'pod', the extra 'spec' key was removed.
    # This ensures the MiniCluster pod is scheduled on a specific AWS instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: "hpc7g.16xlarge"
    # Set the restartPolicy to Never to inspect logs of failed jobs without automatic retries.
    restartPolicy: Never

  # Defines the application container to be run by Flux.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:laghos
      # The command is updated to include the '-pa' flag for performance analysis.
      command: laghos -pa -m cube_311_hex.mesh
      # The launcher flag MUST be false. The Flux Operator is responsible for launch.
      launcher: false

You MUST ensure all globbed files from ./data from the root of the laghos codebase are in the WORKDIR.
